title: Best Security Cameras for Renters (No Drilling Required)
description: Renters need security cameras that don't damage walls. These 5 cameras use magnetic mounts, suction cups, and peel-and-stick installation.
keywords: security cameras for renters, no drill security cameras, renter friendly cameras, apartment security cameras, magnetic mount cameras
content:
Renting does not mean you have to sacrifice security. The biggest concern renters face with security cameras is installation — most landlords prohibit drilling into walls, and security deposits are too expensive to risk losing over a few screw holes. The good news is that the best security cameras for renters in 2026 use magnetic mounts, adjustable stands, suction cups, and peel-and-stick adhesive bases that leave zero damage. Here are the five best options, ranked by value, features, and renter-friendliness.

Why Renters Need Different Cameras

Homeowners can drill anywhere. Renters cannot. Every security camera on this list was chosen because it can be installed and removed without leaving a mark. This means no drill holes, no wall anchors, no adhesive residue, and no lost security deposit. The cameras below use one or more of these damage-free mounting methods:

  • Magnetic mounts — stick to any metal surface instantly (refrigerators, file cabinets, metal door frames)
  • Adjustable stands — sit on shelves, counters, or furniture with no mounting at all
  • Peel-and-stick adhesive — uses removable 3M adhesive strips that pull off cleanly
  • Suction cups — attach to glass windows without residue

Beyond installation, renters should prioritize cameras with local storage options. Cloud subscriptions are optional expenses you do not need. Local storage via microSD cards means your footage stays with you, not tied to a service you might cancel when you move.

Camera 1: Blink Mini 2 ($20, Magnetic Mount)

The Blink Mini 2 is the best value security camera for renters, period. At $20, it costs less than a pizza delivery tip. The magnetic base lets you stick it to any metal surface — a refrigerator, a filing cabinet, a metal shelf bracket — without any tools. It also includes a foldable stand for sitting on flat surfaces.

Key specs: 1080p HD video, two-way audio, motion detection, night vision, works with Alexa. The Blink app provides real-time motion alerts and live view from your phone. You can set custom motion zones so you only get alerts for the areas you care about.

Why renters love it: It is tiny (about 2 inches wide), weighs almost nothing, and the magnetic mount means you can move it room to room in seconds. When you move out, you take it with you. No holes, no residue, no hassle. The optional Blink Subscription Plan is $3/month for cloud storage, but a Sync Module 2 ($35) enables local USB storage with no subscription.

Camera 2: Wyze Cam OG ($20, Indoor Stand)

The Wyze Cam OG matches the Blink Mini 2 on price but offers a different feature set. It uses a simple indoor stand that sits on any flat surface — shelves, desks, countertops, nightstands. No mounting required at all. Just set it down, plug it in, and connect to the app.

Key specs: 1080p HD, color night vision (a significant upgrade over most budget cameras), two-way audio, motion and sound detection. The Wyze app is one of the most feature-rich in the budget category, with customizable motion zones, scheduling, and shared access for family members.

Why renters love it: The stand design means zero installation. You can place it on a bookshelf facing the door, on a kitchen counter facing the living room, or on a windowsill pointing outside. When your lease ends, you pick it up and leave. Wyze also offers free 14-second video clips stored in the cloud, with an optional Cam Plus subscription ($2/month) for longer recordings.

Camera 3: Eufy Solo Indoor 2K ($30, Peel-and-Stick)

The Eufy Solo Indoor 2K steps up resolution to 2K while staying under $30. The standout feature for renters is the peel-and-stick mounting base. The adhesive strip attaches to walls, ceilings, or furniture and removes cleanly with gentle pulling — no tools, no damage.

Key specs: 2K resolution (sharper than 1080p), AI-powered human detection (reduces false alerts from pets and shadows), two-way audio, night vision. Eufy stores footage locally on the camera itself via microSD card, so there is no cloud subscription required. Your footage stays private and local.

Why renters love it: The peel-and-stick base is the most versatile mounting option for renters who want a wall-mounted look without drilling. It holds securely to painted walls, drywall, and most smooth surfaces. When you move, the adhesive pulls off cleanly — test it in a closet first if you are worried. The local storage means no monthly fees, which adds up to real savings over a two-year lease.

Camera 4: Ring Indoor Cam ($60, Adjustable Stand)

Ring is the most recognized name in home security, and the Ring Indoor Cam is their renter-friendly option. The adjustable stand swivels 360 degrees and tilts up and down, letting you aim the camera precisely without mounting anything. It also includes a privacy cover that physically blocks the lens when you are home.

Key specs: 1080p HD, two-way audio, motion detection, Works with Alexa for voice commands and Echo Show live view. Ring's ecosystem is its biggest advantage — if you already have Ring doorbells or Echo devices, the Indoor Cam integrates seamlessly.

Why renters love it: The adjustable stand is the most flexible non-mount option. You can angle it from a bookshelf, desk, or counter to cover any area. The privacy cover is a real feature for renters who share space with roommates or want camera-free time. Ring's app provides real-time alerts and live view, and footage can be stored locally with a Ring Edge microSD card (sold separately) or in the cloud with a Ring Protect subscription ($4/month).

Camera 5: Arlo Essential Indoor ($50, Magnetic Base)

The Arlo Essential Indoor brings premium build quality to the renter-friendly category. The magnetic base attaches to any metal surface, and the camera includes a rechargeable battery, meaning no power cord is required. You can literally stick it anywhere without running cables.

Key specs: 1080p HD, two-way audio, motion detection, color night vision, 100+ dB siren. The siren is a unique feature — you can trigger it remotely from the app to scare off intruders. The rechargeable battery lasts 3-6 months depending on activity level.

Why renters love it: The battery-powered design is the ultimate renter feature. No power cord means no cable management, no outlet limitations, and no visible wires. Stick it on a metal shelf bracket, a refrigerator, a file cabinet, or any ferrous metal surface. The magnetic mount holds securely but pulls off easily when you need to move it. When you leave, there is literally nothing to remove.

Comparison Table

Here is how all five cameras stack up for renters:

Blink Mini 2 ($20) — 1080p, magnetic mount, two-way audio, night vision, Alexa compatible. Best overall value.

Wyze Cam OG ($20) — 1080p, stand mount, two-way audio, color night vision, Wyze app. Best for zero-installation.

Eufy Solo Indoor 2K ($30) — 2K, peel-and-stick, AI human detection, local storage, no subscription. Best resolution.

Ring Indoor Cam ($60) — 1080p, adjustable stand, privacy cover, Alexa ecosystem, live view. Best ecosystem integration.

Arlo Essential Indoor ($50) — 1080p, magnetic base, battery powered, siren, color night vision. Best for wireless freedom.

How to Set Up Without Damaging Walls

Here is the renter-friendly setup process that works for any camera on this list:

Step 1: Choose your locations strategically. Place cameras where they have a clear view of entry points — front door, back door, main living area, and any ground-floor windows. Avoid placing them where they will trigger false alerts from pets, HVAC vents, or street traffic.

Step 2: Use existing surfaces. Bookshelves, countertops, nightstands, and windowsills are your best friends. You do not need to mount anything on a wall. A camera sitting on a shelf aimed at the front door covers the same area as a wall-mounted camera.

Step 3: If you must mount, use peel-and-stick first. Test the adhesive in an inconspicuous area for 24 hours before committing. Most modern adhesive strips (including 3M Command strips) remove cleanly from painted drywall when pulled straight down. Never use nails, screws, or permanent adhesive.

Step 4: Route cables discreetly. If your camera requires a power cord, run it along baseboards, behind furniture, or through door frames using adhesive cable clips. Avoid taping cables to walls, which can peel paint when removed.

Step 5: Test and adjust. Open the app, check the live view, and adjust the camera angle. Most cameras on this list can be repositioned in seconds, so do not be afraid to experiment with placement until you find the optimal angle.
